research_mode: official OSR and ONS sources only; police recorded crime quality oversight, CSEW and police-recorded divergence, current March 2026 measurement boundaries and designation controls; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Quality action plan before reassessment
verified_claims: OSR recommended a joint ONS and Home Office action plan
the plan was intended to address review recommendations
the recommendations were described as critical before reassessment against the Code
limitations: an action plan is not evidence that every recommendation is complete
reassessment status must be checked separately

sources.name: Police recorded crime improvement framework
verified_claims: OSR organised recommendations into three improvement areas
the framework covers data-quality oversight and statistical communication
the framework supports future reassessment
limitations: framework structure is not a force ranking
recommendation coverage does not supply parcel-level outcomes

sources.name: Progress and remaining challenges
verified_claims: OSR recognised substantial progress in crime recording
OSR also identified remaining challenges and oversight gaps
further Home Office and ONS action was requested
limitations: progress since 2014 does not establish uniform current quality
remaining challenges must stay visible in trend interpretation

sources.name: Police workload interpretation
verified_claims: police recorded crime measures crimes reported to and recorded by police
the data can indicate police workload
the series can be reliable for trends in some crime types
limitations: workload is not the same construct as victimisation prevalence
fitness for trend analysis is offence-specific

sources.name: Quality review evidence base
verified_claims: OSR gathered evidence from police forces
HMICFRS was included among stakeholders
ONS and Home Office statisticians also contributed
limitations: stakeholder consultation is not an independent record-level audit
different stakeholders can hold different quality information

sources.name: Comparable crime subset method
verified_claims: ONS adjusted both CSEW and police recorded crime series to form comparable subsets
coverage differences prevent direct use of the full series
the comparison focused on offence types covered by both sources
limitations: the comparable subset is not the complete crime total
adjustments do not make the collection methods identical

sources.name: Comparable-series decline to 2014
verified_claims: both comparable series declined from year ending March 2003 to year ending March 2014
CSEW comparable incidents fell over the period
police recorded comparable offences also fell
limitations: national historical movement is not a parcel-level trajectory
the comparison uses constructed comparable subsets

sources.name: Recording-practice divergence after 2014
verified_claims: the CSEW comparable series generally continued to decrease
police recorded comparable offences rose between year ending March 2015 and March 2019
ONS linked much of the rise to improved recording practices
limitations: recording improvements can increase recorded volumes without equal growth in victimisation
the finding does not exclude genuine change

sources.name: National Crime Recording Standard breakpoint
verified_claims: the National Crime Recording Standard was introduced in April 2002
ONS begins the comparable analysis at year ending March 2003
the standard aimed to improve consistency in police recording
limitations: the standard does not guarantee perfect consistency
pre- and post-standard data require methodological context

sources.name: Possible small-scale over-recording
verified_claims: ONS noted the possibility that some forces may over-record crime in some way
the potential scale was described as small
ONS judged it likely to have minimal impact on the ratio disparity
limitations: possible over-recording must not be assigned to a force without evidence
minimal aggregate impact does not validate individual records
